job: Show who or what something belongs to with initials or a picture.
purpose: A round holder for initials or an image; data-shape="square" gives the soft square used for teams and workspaces. A status dot shows presence. An avatar stack overlaps avatars with a ring in the page colour and ends with an overflow count.
useWhen: A row, comment or card needs the person or team it belongs to.
A list of members is too long to show in full: use a stack ending in a data-overflow count.
Presence matters: add data-status to show online, busy, away or offline.

avoidWhen.when: The holder shows a logo, a brand mark or an icon, not a person.
A person needs a verified seal beside their name.
The label is a word that describes a state, not an identity.

variants.useWhen: A team, workspace or organisation rather than a person.
Inline in dense rows and stacks.
In compact lists and table cells.
In profile headers and large cards.
The current user or the one avatar to notice.
A default fill when no colour has meaning.
Colour a person with a tone that carries meaning, such as active.
A person who needs attention, such as a failed invite.
The "+25" tile at the end of a stack.
The person is not to be interrupted.

parts.role: Overlaps avatars; hover fans them open.
